reviews.title: The new app is trash
reviews.text:
I’m returning all of my battery-powered cameras. If a camera doesn’t record 24/7, you’re stuck with short, six-second clips that are nearly impossible to review properly.

The cameras constantly miss important activity because recording starts too late. When reviewing footage, you can’t pause at the exact moment you want, and you can’t rewind to the beginning without encountering playback errors.

The videos play so quickly that the only thing you can reliably see is the final thumbnail after the clip ends. That defeats the entire purpose of having security cameras.

Whoever designed this playback system seriously needs to rethink it. Fire the engineers responsible for this mess. It’s frustrating, unreliable, and practically useless for security.

I’m returning every one of my cameras.

reviews.title: Good Idea camera, bad app
reviews.text:
The concept of having a second, downward-facing camera specifically for monitoring packages is great. Unfortunately, the Eufy app falls short compared to competitors like Ring, particularly when it comes to motion detection, notification speed, and overall reliability.

Ring consistently delivers notifications faster and with less delay, while also reliably including a thumbnail preview. With Eufy, thumbnail notifications are inconsistent. Sometimes you get an image preview, while other times it’s just a text notification, which is frustrating.

Another issue is how notifications are handled. Sometimes I’ll receive a notification with a thumbnail, but tapping it takes me straight to the live view instead of the recorded event. Even worse, the recording isn’t always available in the Events tab immediately afterward, almost as if it hasn’t finished processing or saving.

Viewing recorded events is another frustration. Recordings are noticeably slow to load, seemingly due to the time it takes the app to decrypt the footage. This makes reviewing motion events unnecessarily tedious, especially when you’re trying to quickly see what triggered a notification.

The hardware and dual-camera concept are promising, but the app experience needs significant improvement. Fast, reliable notifications and quick access to recorded events are basic expectations for a security camera, and Eufy simply isn’t delivering the same level of consistency as Ring.

reviews.title: Step backwards from the old app
reviews.text:
It is buggy, inconsistent, and somehow less reliable than the app it is supposed to replace. Live updates showing device status and progress work when they feel like it. Sometimes they update correctly, sometimes they lag behind, and sometimes they seem completely disconnected from what the device is actually doing.

Even worse, the app will randomly act like devices I have already set up are brand new and try to walk me through setup again. That is not a minor inconvenience. That is basic device management functionality failing.

The most frustrating part is that the old app still works fine. So somehow Eufy managed to replace a functioning app with a worse one, then keeps pushing users toward the new experience anyway.

And then I look at all the glowing 5 star reviews and genuinely feel like the world has lost its mind. Are we all using the same app? Has everyone just collectively decided that broken, buggy, and less functional is good now? I feel like I am living in some bizarre alternate reality where companies make things worse and everyone applauds.

If you are going to force customers onto a replacement app, the replacement should at least be as stable and reliable as the one you are replacing. Right now it is not even close.

The old app works. The new app does not. Yet somehow the new one is the future.

reviews.title: Extremely Disappointed After Years as a Loyal Customer 😡
reviews.text:
I’ve spent thousands of pounds on Anker/Eufy products, including multiple 4K cameras, HomeBase Pro, wall light cams, the E340 doorbell and Floodlight Cam. I’ve been a loyal customer and recommended Eufy to others. 💔

However, for months I’ve faced constant connection and performance problems: cameras disconnect, Wi-Fi is unreliable, notifications are delayed, and live view often remains stuck on “Loading.” 😤

I’ve repeatedly contacted support and provided logs, camera feeds and troubleshooting details, but nothing has resolved the issues. With 2 Gbps broadband, internet speed clearly isn’t the problem. The latest app update has made matters worse, with many customers reporting similar issues. Even the 4K image quality is disappointing, especially when zooming in.

After years of loyalty and significant investment, it’s incredibly frustrating to see a system I once trusted become so unreliable. I have extensive support correspondence and examples, but there’s too much to include here. I genuinely have to ask:

How am I still a customer after all this ? 🤷‍♂️

I hope Anker takes this seriously, because Eufy has gone from something I happily recommended to a product experience that has left me extremely disappointed. 😡💔

reviews.title: Each app date gets worse

Previously if you had more than 20 saved clips on a given day, when you deleted the first 20 it wouldn’t load the remainder. You had to manually refresh. Also every time I open the app at night, it triggers my solo cam S30 to start taking spurious clips. I had upgraded to the home base pro because my previous homebase kept losing connection to my wireless cams. So that doesn’t happen as often with the Pro, but upgrading the internal storage was a disaster. The supplied screws wouldn’t fit a 3.5” HDD so you can’t attach it to the supplied sled. Using an adapter I finally got a 2.5” SSD to work. Of course the adapter is not supplied. But it seems that with every app “update” things get worse.

reviews.title: It’s Gimmicky…
reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars I would. I have 7 Eufy products, and 3 different kinds of video recording devices from them. In all of them, you can’t scrub the footage natively in the app. Meaning if you’re watching a recording that’s say, 40 seconds long and 20 seconds in you want to go back to the 15 second mark to view something, you can’t. You can only play and pause the video. You cannot rewind or fast forward; jump back or skip forward. So you’d have to close the recording, then reopen it to replay it from the beginning 🙄 and then try to pause it at the 15 second mark that you’re trying to view again. 🙄 Not only are you UNABLE to go back/ rewind a recording, but you are also UNABLE to jump ahead. Eufy, what is the point of having a video length bar, if we’re not allowed to utilize it?!?! To be able to replay parts we’ve watched to review something, or jump ahead in footage we would have to download the recordings which is unnecessary and time consuming, ESPECIALLY when we’ve spent money buying a HomeBase 3 AND external storage in the home base. 🙄 Eufy PLEASE FIX THIS! This is kind of ridiculous and you’re making me consider reinstalling my Ring doorbell. This is a BASIC feature that all your competitors have natively in their apps.

reviews.title: Cumberson, clunky
reviews.text: I find the eufy application is increasingly difficult to use, with the obvious focus on Marketing rather than on quality user experience.  In the early days, this app was one of the best - it was friendly, easy to navigate, really quick and realy simple. One of its best features was that, if the doorbell rang, there were not a lot of steps to get to the camera view to see who is at the door.  (That IS, after all, why this app even exists, regardless what marketing might think!  And that IS why we spend our money...)  But over time it has devolved into a cumbersone app - especially with regard to the bloat-filled startup.  More times than not, I am greeted with a Login page, where I have to enter a password I don't remember (the app refuses to offer password saving after all these years).  Although I have Face ID set, this app (and none of my others) seems to have a problem with Face ID - it works about 50% of the time.  In the end, I usually spend about two minutes figuing out the password and getting logged in.  Once I'm logged in, I am greeted with an _old_ view from the camera (why?) and have to click on it for a live view. By the time all this has happened - the guest is either gone or as frustrated as me.  Useless!

reviews.title: Purchase at your and your family’s risk 🛑✋
reviews.text:
Rating: 1/5 Stars

Save your money. Save your sanity. And whatever you do, do not trust this lock with your family's safety.

I am the fool who bought this product twice. The first lock was a gift for my fiancée, a symbol of protection for the people I love most. Instead, it delivered nothing but frustration, sleepless nights, and hours of my life I will never get back. The fingerprint scanner? A complete failure from day one. It never worked. Not once.

After an exhausting back-and-forth with customer service countless emails that led absolutely nowhere they threw me a 30% discount as a peace offering. And like a desperate, hopeful idiot, I accepted. I convinced myself the "new and improved" version would be different. That this company had learned from its mistakes.

They hadn't. And neither had I.

This second lock suffers from the exact same fatal flaw. It refuses to connect to Wi-Fi no matter how many hours I wasted on the phone with T-Mobile, AT&T, EarthLink, believing I was the problem. Believing my internet was the weak link. But no. The weak link is this far from cheap, unreliable, janky excuse for a security device.

Do not make my mistake. Do not let a discount blind you to the truth. This company doesn't care about your safety they care about your wallet. They will sell you the same broken dream in a new box and call it an upgrade.

Save your money. Save your peace of mind. Buy literally anything else. And stay far, far away from this company.

reviews.title: Frustrating and extremely disappointing
reviews.text:
Considering how much money we’ve spent on these cameras, we expected them to work properly and for the app to be quick, reliable, and high functioning — especially given these are some of the most expensive cameras you sell. Unfortunately, that has not been our experience at all.
The system is constantly plagued by lag, delays, loading issues, crashes, glitches, and missing footage. Trying to review events is often incredibly frustrating, with repeated “no events for this day” messages even when footage should clearly exist.
The doorbell camera in particular misses huge chunks of important activity despite the settings being adjusted correctly. For example, I can leave the house, walk to the car, return to the house, and large parts — or sometimes all — of that activity are simply not captured.
More concerningly, something was recently stolen from a neighbour right outside the back of our house. The cameras had been recording and detecting people consistently throughout the entire day up until that exact period of time, yet for around an hour the system completely failed. No footage was available, no events were shown, and nothing was captured during the exact timeframe we actually needed the cameras to work. That is completely unacceptable for a security system at this price point.
Trying to check live footage when something is happening in real time can take several minutes to load, which completely defeats the purpose of having security cameras in the first place. Looking

reviews.title: Cumbersome needs desperate work!!
reviews.text:

reviews.title: Unusable notifications!
reviews.text: The thing that makes Eufy terrible is its dumb notification system. It’s SO bad that they take over your phone and you have to completely disable them. You can’t mute them, and it just peppers your phone with notifications meaning you can’t use your phone for anything else.  Solution - you have to completely disable notifications because the dumb software doesn’t let you set it to mute repeat notifications. Really dumb guys. So my advice is avoid Eufy until they one day improve their software. Many other issues but that’s the biggest one.

reviews.title: Devolved as an App
reviews.text: When I first downloaded this app ~2 years ago, it was good. Everything worked efficiently, loaded well, etc. At some point, that all changed. I think it came a few updates in when the notifications switched from “motion detected” to “someone has been spotted”. Odd verbiage. No big deal. Except for the fact that nothing really works now? In The Old Days, when I tapped on a notification it would take me straight to the recorded segment of whatever happened. Now it just takes you to the home screen, making you click to get to the recording section, only to find that the segment hasn’t populated yet. I got a notification today for movement, and it took another 20 minutes for that recording to populate in my activity page despite multiple new notifications. What? Why? You guys got it right two years ago-so what compelled you to change your perfectly functioning app? It also has a 50/50 chance of detecting a package. You know, the thing I bought it for. And if a package is placed further than a foot from the camera, every subsequent motion notification sends the ominous notification that “your package has been moved”, even if it’s just someone walking by, not having even glanced at my package. To the people developing this app, figure it out.

reviews.title: Good hardware, meh software
reviews.text: Eufy hardware seems capable, well-made, and reasonably priced. However, the product line fails to completely satisfy because the software is not completely useful. There is AI face recognition, which is a nod to the hype around AI, but they don’t seem to understand the use cases that a homeowner would value. I have a choice of getting notifications and recording about everything, or nothing. What I want is to not be informed when somebody walks by on the sidewalk, but I do want to be informed when somebody comes to the door. If I don’t have the “bother me about everything” mode enabled, I won’t even get an event, much less an image capture or recording, if somebody rings the doorbell. Just today the Eufy doorbell was rung; I could see that it was two men, but I was unable to answer the door. Later I had no record of that event. If a package is left on my front steps, Eufy won’t tell me about it unless I have the “bother me about everything” mode enabled. The visual scene for somebody walking by on the sidewalk is very different from the visual scene of somebody approaching my door. I would think that AI would be capable of classifying these events pretty well. I assume Eufy is a company of technologists, and not user experience people.

reviews.title: Used to be good
reviews.text:

However, almost every day the app automatically switches the camera back to HomeBase 3 instead of staying on the selected WiFi network. reviews.title: Unusable!
reviews.text:
When I first purchased my Eufy Video Doorbell E340, the app worked perfectly. Unfortunately, since the version 5.0 update, performance has steadily declined, and each update seems to make things worse rather than better.

When someone rings my doorbell, I receive a notification, but opening the live view can take up to 60 seconds or more. By the time the video finally loads, the person at the door has usually already left. Recorded clips can now take up to five minutes to appear, which completely defeats the purpose of having a smart doorbell.

Since updating to version 5.6.00, the app has become even less reliable. I now receive no notifications at all when someone approaches or rings the doorbell. This issue affects all of my devices and started immediately after updating the app.

What is particularly frustrating is that the adverts within the app load instantly and work perfectly, with no delays whatsoever, while core features such as live view, recordings, and notifications are painfully slow or non-functional. It gives the impression that advertising is being prioritised over the customer experience.

I paid a significant amount of money for this system, and it is extremely disappointing to see its functionality degraded through software updates rather than improved.

reviews.title: Doorbell camera not quite good enough
reviews.text:
The doorbell camera takes way too long to register and when it enviably notifies you that there’s someone at the door, the person has either moved away (especially with delivery drivers) who haven’t got all day to wait for your camera to pick them up and for you to eventually respond!

Them images from the camera are ok but field of view and the time it takes for the camera to register images, notify you, then open the app and for you to eventually have a meaningful conversation with the person at the door requires huge improvement and is the main massive let down for all versions of Eufy doorbell cameras!

reviews.title: Recordings inaccessible if camera is gone
reviews.text:
The UI could use a little help:  when viewing a video feed, let a swipe down motion anywhere on the screen be equivalent to tapping the back arrow, as those arrows can be finicky to hit and a simple swipe would be fast and convenient. Let swiping left and right move the view to the next and previous cameras, respectively. 

Regardless of whether recordings are stored in the base or in Eufy’s cloud, if a camera goes offline for any reason (hardware failure, stolen, loss of signal, etc.), recordings for that camera are totally inaccessible until the camera is restored (if ever). A worst-case scenario would be a thief steals the cameras and no video evidence is available. This is utterly ridiculous behavior to the point that it seems Eufy intended it this way. The cameras are often poor at reliably detecting and recording motion events to begin with. Look elsewhere for real security!
UPDATE: Eufy support sent an irrelevant response to this review. Their response was all about HomeKit integration. I don’t use HomeKit, my review doesn’t mention it, and the failure mentioned here has nothing to do with HomeKit.
